t: You're looking at Academy Gardens, a Neo-Georgian apartment complex on Duchess of Bedford's Walk in Kensington. It was built in 1914 as Queen Elizabeth College, the Ladies' Department of King's College, London. Two architects designed it. Henry Percy Adams specialised in planning hospitals. Charles Holden, his fellow designer here, went on to become best known for London Underground stations in the 1920s and 1930s, and for Senate House at the University of London. Today the building is homes rather than a college.
